title: Regional utilization optimizer and holdback calculator — Private VPC capacity planning (2026)
summary: Working worksheet to size Private/VPC GPU fleets across regions with an explicit holdback (spare) capacity lane for failover, upgrades, and cache-warmup. Includes node-mix tradeoffs and three demand scenarios (steady, burst, phased-growth).
purpose: Provide SRE/infra and sales/ops a pragmatic calculator to convert customer peak/avg qps and model token profiles into a recommended node purchase plan by region, including recommended holdback %, replacement cadence, and cost bands for procurement discussions.
high_level_methodology: 1) Normalize incoming workload to GPU-token throughput required; 2) Apply target utilization and scaling headroom to compute active fleet size; 3) Add holdback buffer lanes (for failover / prewarming / upgrades); 4) Translate to node counts by preferred GPU SKU mix (H100/A100/L40 where applicable); 5) Compute CapEx/Opex for procurement windows and ramp schedule.
inputs: avg_tokens_per_request: average tokens generated per request
tokens_per_gpu_sec_by_sku: measured tokens/sec per GPU SKU (user provides per-SKU profile)
burst_headroom_multiplier: additional capacity for short spikes (default 1.35)
holdback_percent: % of fleet held as spare buffer for upgrades/failover (default 12%)
region_locality_penalty: latency/regulatory constraint multiplier (1.0 for none)
model_mix_weighting: percent distribution across heavy/medium/light models (affects tokens/sec)
cache_warm_preload_factor: extra capacity needed to warm KV/prefix caches after rollout (use 0.1-0.25)
planned_deprecation_window_months: months to retire older nodes (affects staggered purchasing)
desired_redundancy_zones: number of AZs to distribute across (default 3)
core_formulas_and_calcs: effective_tokens_capacity_per_gpu = tokens_per_gpu_sec_by_sku * 3600 * average_request_duration_seconds / 3600 (use measured tokens/sec directly when available)
scenarios: Conservative steady: target_util=60%, holdback=15%, burst=1.2 => minimizes risk, higher capex
Balanced default: target_util=65%, holdback=12%, burst=1.35 => recommended for most private deployments
Aggressive cost-opt: target_util=72%, holdback=8%, burst=1.25 => lower upfront cost, higher operational risk
Phased growth: start with 60% utilization and scale quarterly based on telemetry; holdback starts at 20% during first 3 months for burn-in
capacity_matrix_rows: region, demand_fraction, preferred_sku, gpus_per_node, tokens_per_gpu_sec, avg_util_target, burst_mul, holdback_pct, nodes_required
recommended_bom: Node SKU A: 8x H100 (PCIe/HBM gen?) — best for high-throughput low-latency heavy models; recommended for primary hot lanes in US-west-2
Node SKU B: 8x A100 — cost-effective middle ground for steady inference workloads in EU regions
Node SKU C: 8x L40s — good for lower-cost inference and specialized LLM variants in APAC or for embedding-heavy workloads
Network: dual-100Gbps per node leaf topology; 2x redundant TORs per rack
Storage: NVMe local scratch per node for KV cache (1–2TB) + NFS/CEPH backplane for checkpoints
Other: KMS/HSM integration nodes (2 per region for key redundancy), management jump hosts (1 per AZ)
procurement_and_cost_bands: Estimate method: use list price * node_count then apply negotiated discount band (5–18%) and add 8% for spares + freight/installation
Example cost band (per-node rough): H100-8x node ~ $70k list, A100-8x node ~ $46k list, L40-8x node ~ $28k list
Three-year view: include maintenance contract (~6%/yr), electricity estimate by region (use local rate), and uplift for capacity headroom during first 6 months
Opex considerations: GPU leases vs purchase, managed support add-on, and on-call ops team burn during initial ramp
assumptions: tokens_per_gpu_sec measured from internal perf harness (if missing, use conservative public benchmarks and validate in staging)
Regional demand fractions sum to 1.0; if not, scale proportionally
Network fabric can scale linearly with node additions; if not, add dedicated spine upgrades in the first procurement window
Holdback lane is primarily used for prewarming caches and rolling upgrades, not for day-to-day autoscale
We assume a 3-month lead time for procurement baseline; add 8–16 weeks for custom racks or constrained SKUs
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Underestimated token rate for emergent models => Mitigation: instrument detailed telemetry + add an emergency burst pool in a paired region
Risk: SKU supply delays => Mitigation: diversify node mix across 2 SKUs and keep 10% extra budget for spot purchases
Risk: Overcommitment leading to wasted CapEx => Mitigation: staged purchases (quarterly) and leverage short-term dedicated capacity for first 9 months

notes_and_tips: Tip: Treat holdback nodes as a separate lane in the scheduler so they are not consumed by normal autoscaling policies
Tip: Use pre-warm jobs during low-traffic windows to populate KV and reduce cold-start burst requirements
Operational note: Staggered deprecation windows reduce simultaneous capacity churn — aim for <= 20% of nodes cycled per month
